clue.text: Like a little doctor's treatment in Ireland

definitions.text: Like a little doctor's treatment in Ireland

blocks.note: surface reading: a modest dose of medicine, the way a doctor might prescribe it
setter's reading: a place in Ireland that shares its name with a famous television doctor

explanation.surface: A gentle medical treatment being given somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Kildare was the young hero of a popular 1960s television hospital drama; Kildare is also a county in Ireland, so the doctor's name points to the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The county lying west of Dublin carries the same surname as the fictional young physician, which is the whole joke.

clue.text: Incorrectly parked in outside car-park -- it's criminal!

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters are set out wrongly and must be rearranged
outside says the rearranged letters stand around the abbreviation

blocks.note: the eight letters rearranged
P is the map and road-sign symbol for a car park

explanation.surface: Someone who parks badly by a car park is told off as a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parked in' looks like boxed in by another car; the words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper abducts and holds people for ransom, a serious crime, so the noun fits.

clue.text: "Room at the Top" occupying the French screen

indicators.note: occupying means living inside, so the room goes within the article

blocks.note: le is the French for the
an attic is the room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: The film 'Room at the Top' being shown on a cinema screen in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room at the Top' is a famous 1959 British film, but here it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross frame of strips used as a screen or partition.

clue.text: Directs a dunderhead over clothes

indicators.note: the head of a word is its beginning, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
read as dunder plus head: the head, or first letter, of dunder
dresses are clothes

explanation.surface: Someone instructs a fool about what to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' splits as dunder plus head, the first letter. In a down clue 'over' places one part above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a letter is to direct it, writing where it should go, and to address remarks is to aim them.

clue.text: A nymph's sound reflection

blocks.note: first meaning: the mountain nymph of Greek myth who pined away for Narcissus
second meaning: a sound bouncing back off a surface

explanation.surface: A woodland spirit sees her own sound bounced back to her.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, in the myth the nymph was left only able to repeat others' last words.
explanation.definitionFit: Myth names the nymph Echo, and physics calls a reflected sound wave by the same word.

clue.text: Foreign money is the making of him

blocks.note: the franc was the currency of France, Belgium and Switzerland
taken as written

explanation.surface: Inherited money from abroad turned someone into a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The making of him' reads as a phrase about success; it actually says the pieces make up a man, whose name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis is a man's first name, so a pronoun for any male person can stand in for it.

clue.text: Lots may be so hostile

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words
second meaning: unfriendly and threatening in appearance

explanation.surface: Many people may be unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like a crowd of people; it means items at an auction, put up for offers.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction lot is offered so buyers can bid, and a grim stern look is described as forbidding.

clue.text: Spoken — spoken as permitted

indicators.note: spoken says the next word is to be heard, not read

blocks.note: permitted means allowed, which is said the same way

explanation.surface: Someone told they may speak at last says their words out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'spoken' is deliberate: the first is the definition, the second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Words said out loud rather than thought or written are uttered, voiced audibly.

clue.text: Hand without trumps makes trick

blocks.note: first meaning: in bridge and whist, a hand dealt with no cards of the trump suit
second meaning: trickery or deception, chicanery

explanation.surface: A card player with no trumps still takes a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Card language in the surface suggests winning a trick at bridge; 'trick' instead means a deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge term for a trumpless hand is also an old word for deceitful dealing or a ruse.

clue.text: Begin to jump

blocks.note: first meaning: to commence
second meaning: to flinch suddenly in surprise

explanation.surface: An instruction to commence leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to commence something, and also to give a sudden involuntary movement from fright.

clue.text: Taken out, being rather old

blocks.note: first meaning: escorted on a romantic outing
second meaning: old-fashioned, past its time

explanation.surface: Someone escorted somewhere despite being a bit past it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out romantically is to go on dates with them, and something old-fashioned is said to look past its era.

clue.text: Damage with a coin maybe, or a small instrument

indicators.note: maybe says the letters given might be some other arrangement of themselves

blocks.note: to damage is to harm
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Scratching something with a coin, or perhaps a tiny musical instrument instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is a small handheld wind instrument played by blowing and drawing air through reeds.

clue.text: A team's remarks not generally overhead

blocks.note: taken as written
a team is a side, and with the possessive it becomes side's, read as plain letters

explanation.surface: Comments made by members of a sports team that nobody else catches.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper printed 'overhead', a misprint for 'overheard'. The apostrophe in 'team's' is ignored, as crossword punctuation often is.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre an aside is a remark spoken for the audience that other characters on stage supposedly cannot hear.

clue.text: 27 appearing in film that is improperly distributed

indicators.note: something appearing in another thing turns up inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a film of condensation or haze is a mist
27 across is TRADE, and to trade is to deal

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that seems to be about a business shown in a film that was badly released.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' points at the answer to 27 across, which must be swapped for a synonym before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Misdealing is handing out cards wrongly, so cards misdealt have been given out in an improper way.

clue.text: Public officer coping with a trying job

definitions.text: Public officer coping with a trying job

blocks.note: surface reading: an official struggling with a stressful, difficult post
setter's reading: trying means hearing court cases, the core of this official's work

explanation.surface: A civil servant struggling with a stressful position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' reads as exhausting; it is the work of judging defendants in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice of the peace who hears minor criminal cases in a lower court tries defendants as a job.

clue.text: Iron in cupboard

blocks.note: first meaning: to smooth clothes flat
second meaning: a large cupboard, especially for linen, in older or Irish use

explanation.surface: An iron kept stored away in a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes is ironing them, and a linen press is a tall storage cupboard for sheets and towels.

clue.text: Stars with capital going to American lawyer

blocks.note: with means together with, plus
the capital of Italy
a district attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Celebrities who have money hiring a lawyer from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' and 'capital' suggest film stars and wealth; here they are a constellation and a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a northern constellation, a named group of stars, and also the galaxy that lies within it.

clue.text: Chipping, for example, a great painting

blocks.note: first meaning: Mr Chipping, the aged schoolmaster of the novel Goodbye, Mr Chips
second meaning: a picture by a leading European artist before about 1800

explanation.surface: Chipping paint, say, on a valuable canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: Chipping looks like flaking paint; it is the surname of Mr Chips in James Hilton's novel, an elderly teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly teacher can be called this, and so can a canvas by a pre-modern European artist of renown.

clue.text: Putting a point about Navy ratings decoration

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the dot goes around the sailors

blocks.note: taken as written
a point is a dot
the Royal Navy
ratings are ordinary sailors, the men below officer rank

explanation.surface: Applying a mark next to a Navy sailor's medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' looks like scores; in the Royal Navy a rating is a sailor who is not an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adornment is an ornament or embellishment added to make something look finer.

clue.text: Servicemen calling for some relaxation

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a calling or vocation in life

explanation.surface: Soldiers asking for a little rest and recreation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' reads as shouting out; it is a noun meaning vocation.
explanation.definitionFit: A remission is a lessening or easing, as when an illness abates or a penalty is reduced.

clue.text: Low — right time for a tie-up

blocks.note: a cow lows, making a moo
R is the abbreviation for right
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Feeling down, waiting for the ideal moment to secure a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for being sad; it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a boat ties it up, and the place or charge for doing so is the moorage.

clue.text: After a row walk the dog

indicators.note: after places one piece following another, so the noise comes first

blocks.note: a row, rhyming with how, is a loud noise or din
to walk is to go

explanation.surface: Taking the dog out for a walk to calm down after an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk the dog' reads as one chore; the dog is the definition and walk is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog of Australia, a species of canine.

clue.text: Tore up class report

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: tore along means ran fast
a class or grade is a rate, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Ripping up a school report card in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tore up' reads as ripping paper; tore means sped.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give an account of events, to tell or report them.

clue.text: A river and country rat

blocks.note: taken as written
the Po is the longest river in Italy
a country or nation is a state

explanation.surface: A rodent living along a river out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country rat' reads as a rural rodent; rat here is a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in slang is a deserter or traitor, and an apostate abandons a faith or cause.

clue.text: Limits a large number just a little

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular answer: ambit means the bounds or scope of something

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone restricts a big figure only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or extent of something, the boundary within which it operates.

clue.text: Pick-me-up for heavyweight in charge

blocks.note: a ton is a heavy weight
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A restorative drink for a boxer who is in command.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine or drink taken to restore energy and spirits.

clue.text: She's far from bright — backing neither alternative

indicators.note: backing means moving back, so the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: matt (also spelt mat) describes a dull surface without shine
nor is the word that follows neither, offering the second alternative

explanation.surface: A woman who is not very clever and won't pick either option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from bright' looks like a dig at someone's intelligence; it means dull in finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a married woman of dignified standing, or a senior nurse, so a female pronoun can stand for her.

clue.text: Watch money gradually leak away

blocks.note: to watch is to see
p is the abbreviation for a penny or pence

explanation.surface: Observe your savings slowly draining away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch money' sounds like keeping an eye on finances, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that seeps oozes slowly through small openings, escaping little by little.

clue.text: The head will get personal support in a lawsuit

blocks.note: a bra supports the wearer's body
taken as written
a lawsuit is a case in court

explanation.surface: The boss receives private backing in the middle of litigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' sounds like a headteacher or boss; it is the part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The braincase is the cranium, the bony part of the skull enclosing the brain, so it is the top of the body loosely.

clue.text: Rated perhaps as skilled work

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters given might stand in some other order

blocks.note: its five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A job valued as one that needs expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled manual occupation such as plumbing or carpentry, learned by apprenticeship.

clue.text: Sweet stuff will be found in the centre -- a clear liquid

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the following words already

blocks.note: the last three letters of centre, then a, then the first three of clear
surface padding that completes the picture of a runny filling

explanation.surface: A sweet that has a runny clear filling in its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' only completes the picture; treacle, a dark sugar syrup, is a liquid itself, which makes the clue fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick syrup made in sugar refining, eaten as a sweetener or in desserts such as tart.

clue.text: Drink about ten? That's a bad sign

indicators.note: about means going around, so the drink wraps the number

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asking if it's acceptable to have a drink around ten o'clock, then worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About ten' reads as roughly ten o'clock; about is the instruction to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen, usually of something momentous or calamitous to come.
